notes: appearance_source preserves the BJCP Appearance text used as the source.
Structured values are normalized for the application; null means the Appearance text does not provide that parameter explicitly.
lacing is true only when lacing/lace is explicitly stated in the Appearance text; otherwise false.

styles.name: American Light Lager
styles.appearance_source: Very pale straw to pale yellow color. White, frothy head seldom persists. Very clear.

styles.name: American Lager
styles.appearance_source: Very pale straw to medium yellow color. White, frothy head seldom persists. Very clear.

styles.name: Cream Ale
styles.appearance_source: Pale straw to light gold color, although usually on the pale side. Low to medium head with medium to high carbonation. Fair head retention. Brilliant, sparkling clarity. Effervescent.

styles.name: American Wheat Beer
styles.appearance_source: Usually pale yellow to gold. Clarity may range from brilliant to hazy with yeast approximating a Weissbier. Big, long-lasting white head.

styles.name: International Pale Lager
styles.appearance_source: Pale straw to gold color. White, frothy head may not be long lasting. Very clear.

styles.name: International Amber Lager
styles.appearance_source: Golden-amber to reddish-copper color. Bright clarity. White to off-white foam stand which may not last.

styles.name: International Dark Lager
styles.appearance_source: Deep amber to very dark brown with bright clarity and ruby highlights. Foam stand may not be long lasting, and is beige to light tan in color.

styles.name: Czech Pale Lager
styles.appearance_source: Light yellow to deep gold color. Brilliant to very clear, with a long-lasting, creamy white head.

styles.name: Czech Premium Pale Lager
styles.appearance_source: Medium yellow to deep gold color. Brilliant to very clear clarity. Dense, long-lasting, creamy white head.

styles.name: Czech Amber Lager
styles.appearance_source: Deep amber to copper color. Clear to bright clarity. Large, off-white, persistent head.

styles.name: Czech Dark Lager
styles.appearance_source: Dark copper to almost black color, often with a red or garnet tint. Clear to bright clarity. Large, off-white to tan, persistent head.

styles.name: Munich Helles
styles.appearance_source: Pale yellow to pale gold. Clear. Persistent creamy white head.

styles.name: Festbier
styles.appearance_source: Deep yellow to deep gold color; should not have amber hues. Bright clarity. Persistent white to off-white foam stand. Most commercial examples are pale gold in color.

styles.name: Helles Bock
styles.appearance_source: Deep gold to light amber in color. Bright to clear clarity. Large, creamy, persistent, white head.

styles.name: German Leichtbier
styles.appearance_source: Pale straw to deep yellow in color. Brilliant clarity. Moderate white head with average to below average persistence.

styles.name: Kölsch
styles.appearance_source: Medium yellow to light gold. Brilliant clarity. Has a delicate white head that may not persist.

styles.name: German Helles Exportbier
styles.appearance_source: Medium yellow to deep gold. Clear. Persistent white head.

styles.name: German Pils
styles.appearance_source: Straw to deep yellow, brilliant to very clear, with a creamy, long-lasting white head.

styles.name: Märzen
styles.appearance_source: Amber-orange to deep reddish-copper color; should not be golden. Bright clarity, with persistent, off-white foam stand.

styles.name: Rauchbier
styles.appearance_source: Very clear, with a large, creamy, rich, tan- to cream-colored head. Deep amber to coppery-brown in color, often a little darker than the underlying Märzen style.

styles.name: Dunkles Bock
styles.appearance_source: Light copper to brown color, often with attractive garnet highlights. Good clarity despite the dark color. Large, creamy, persistent, off-white head.

styles.name: Vienna Lager
styles.appearance_source: Light reddish amber to copper color. Bright clarity. Large, off-white, persistent head.

styles.name: Altbier
styles.appearance_source: The color ranges from amber to deep copper, stopping short of brown; bronze-orange is most common. Brilliant clarity. Thick, creamy, long-lasting off-white head.

styles.name: Munich Dunkel
styles.appearance_source: Deep copper to dark brown, often with a red or garnet tint. Creamy, light to medium tan head. Usually clear.

styles.name: Schwarzbier
styles.appearance_source: Medium to very dark brown in color, often with deep ruby to garnet highlights, yet almost never truly black. Very clear. Large, persistent, tan-colored head.

styles.name: Doppelbock
styles.appearance_source: Good clarity, with a large, creamy, persistent head. Dark versions are copper to dark brown in color, often with ruby highlights, and an off-white head. Pale versions are deep gold to light amber in color, with a white head.

styles.name: Eisbock
styles.appearance_source: Deep copper to dark brown in color, often with attractive ruby highlights. Good clarity. Head retention may be moderate to poor. Off-white to deep ivory colored head. Pronounced legs are often evident.

styles.name: Baltic Porter
styles.appearance_source: Dark reddish-copper to opaque dark brown color, but not black. Thick, persistent tan-colored head. Clear, although darker versions can be opaque.

styles.name: Weissbier
styles.appearance_source: Pale straw to gold in color. Very thick, moussy, long-lasting white head. Can be hazy and have a shine from wheat and yeast, although this can settle out in bottles.

styles.name: Dunkles Weissbier
styles.appearance_source: Light copper to dark, mahogany brown in color. Very thick, moussy, long-lasting off-white head. Can be hazy and have a shine from wheat and yeast, although this can settle out in bottled versions.

styles.name: Weizenbock
styles.appearance_source: Very thick, moussy, long-lasting head. Can be hazy and have a shine from wheat and yeast, although this can settle out with age. Dark versions are dark amber to dark ruby-brown in color, with a light tan head. Pale versions are gold to amber in color, with a very white to off-white head.

styles.name: Ordinary Bitter
styles.appearance_source: Pale amber to light copper color. Good to brilliant clarity. Low to moderate white to off-white head. May have very little head due to low carbonation.

styles.name: Best Bitter
styles.appearance_source: Pale amber to medium copper color. Good to brilliant clarity. Low to moderate white to off-white head. May have very little head due to low carbonation.

styles.name: Strong Bitter
styles.appearance_source: Light amber to deep copper color. Good to brilliant clarity. Low to moderate white to off-white head. A low head is acceptable when carbonation is also low.

styles.name: British Golden Ale
styles.appearance_source: Straw to golden in color. Good to brilliant clarity. Low to moderate white head. A low head is acceptable when carbonation is also low.

styles.name: Australian Sparkling Ale
styles.appearance_source: Deep yellow to light amber in color, often medium gold. Tall, frothy, persistent white head with tiny bubbles. Noticeable effervescence due to high carbonation. Brilliant clarity if decanted, but typically poured with yeast to have a cloudy appearance. Not typically cloudy unless yeast roused during the pour.

styles.name: English IPA
styles.appearance_source: Color ranges from golden to deep amber, but most are fairly pale. Should be clear, although unfiltered dry- hopped versions may be a bit hazy. Moderate-sized, persistent head stand with off-white color.

styles.name: Dark Mild
styles.appearance_source: Copper to dark brown or mahogany color. Generally clear, although is traditionally unfiltered. Low to moderate off-white to tan head; retention may be poor.

styles.name: British Brown Ale
styles.appearance_source: Dark amber to dark reddish-brown color. Clear. Low to moderate off-white to light tan head.

styles.name: English Porter
styles.appearance_source: Brown to dark brown in color, often with ruby highlights. Good clarity, although may be opaque. Moderate off-white to light tan head with good to fair retention.

styles.name: Scottish Light
styles.appearance_source: Deep copper to dark brown. Clear. Low to moderate, creamy off-white.

styles.name: Scottish Heavy
styles.appearance_source: Pale copper to brown. Clear. Low to moderate, creamy off-white.

styles.name: Scottish Export
styles.appearance_source: Pale copper to brown. Clear. Low to moderate, creamy off-white.

styles.name: Irish Red Ale
styles.appearance_source: Medium amber to medium reddish-copper color. Clear. Low off-white to tan colored head, average persistence.

styles.name: Irish Stout
styles.appearance_source: Jet black to deep brown with garnet highlights in color. According to Guinness, “Guinness beer may appear black, but it is actually a very dark shade of ruby.” Opaque. A thick, creamy, long-lasting, tan- to brown-colored head is characteristic when served on nitro, but don’t expect a tight, creamy head on a bottled beer.

styles.name: Irish Extra Stout
styles.appearance_source: Jet black. Opaque. A thick, creamy, persistent tan head is characteristic.

styles.name: Sweet Stout
styles.appearance_source: Very dark brown to black in color. Clear, if not opaque. Creamy tan to brown head.

styles.name: Oatmeal Stout
styles.appearance_source: Brown to black in color. Thick, creamy, persistent tan- to brown-colored head. Clear, if not opaque.

styles.name: Tropical Stout
styles.appearance_source: Very deep brown to black in color. Clarity usually obscured by deep color. Clear, if not opaque. Large tan to brown head with good retention.

styles.name: Foreign Extra Stout
styles.appearance_source: Very deep brown to black in color. Clarity usually obscured by deep color. Clear, if not opaque. Large tan to brown head with good retention.

styles.name: British Strong Ale
styles.appearance_source: Amber to dark reddish-brown color; many are fairly dark. Generally clear, although darker versions may be almost opaque. Moderate to low cream- to light tan-colored head with average retention.

styles.name: Old Ale
styles.appearance_source: Deep amber to very dark reddish-brown color, but most are fairly dark. Age and oxidation may darken the beer further. Clear, but can be almost opaque. Moderate to low cream- to light tan-colored head; retention average to poor.

styles.name: Wee Heavy
styles.appearance_source: Light copper to dark brown color, often with deep ruby highlights. Clear. Usually has a large tan head, which may not persist. Legs may be evident in stronger versions.

styles.name: English Barley Wine
styles.appearance_source: Color ranging from golden amber to dark brown, often with ruby highlights and significant depth of color. Should not be black or opaque. Low to moderate off- white head. May have low head retention. Brilliant clarity, particularly when aged, although younger versions can have a little haze. High alcohol and viscosity may be visible as legs.

styles.name: Blonde Ale
styles.appearance_source: Light yellow to deep gold in color. Clear to brilliant. Low to medium white head with fair to good retention.

styles.name: American Pale Ale
styles.appearance_source: Pale golden to amber. Moderately large white to off-white head with good retention. Generally quite clear.

styles.name: American Amber Ale
styles.appearance_source: Deep amber to coppery-brown in color, sometimes with a reddish hue. Moderately large off-white head with good retention. Generally quite clear.

styles.name: California Common
styles.appearance_source: Medium amber to light copper color. Generally clear. Moderate off-white head with good retention.

styles.name: American Brown Ale
styles.appearance_source: Light to very dark brown color. Clear. Low to moderate off-white to light tan head.

styles.name: American Porter
styles.appearance_source: Medium brown to very dark brown, often with ruby- or garnet-like highlights. Can approach black in color. Clear, if not opaque. Full, tan-colored head with moderately good head retention.

styles.name: American Stout
styles.appearance_source: Generally a jet black color, although some may appear very dark brown. Large, persistent head of light tan to light brown in color. Usually opaque.

styles.name: Imperial Stout
styles.appearance_source: Color ranges from very dark reddish-brown to jet black. Opaque. Deep tan to dark brown head. Generally has a well-formed head, although head retention may be low to moderate. High alcohol and viscosity may be visible as legs.

styles.name: American IPA
styles.appearance_source: Color ranging from medium gold to light reddish-amber. Clear, but light haze allowable. Medium-sized, white to off-white head with good persistence.

styles.name: Specialty IPA
styles.appearance_source: Color depends on specific type of Specialty IPA. Most should be clear, but a slight haze is acceptable in most styles. Darker types can be opaque, making clarity irrelevant. Good, persistent head stand with color dependent on the specific type of Specialty IPA.

styles.name: Hazy IPA
styles.appearance_source: Color ranging from straw to very light amber, sometimes with an orange hue. Hazy, often opaque, clarity; should not be cloudy or murky. The opacity can add a ‘shine’ to the beer and make the color seem darker. Any visible floating hop matter, yeast clumps, or other particulates is a fault. Medium to rocky, meringue-like white head with high to very high retention.

styles.name: Double IPA
styles.appearance_source: Gold to light orange-copper color, but most modern versions are fairly pale. Good clarity, although a little haze is acceptable. Moderate-sized, persistent, white to off- white head.

styles.name: American Strong Ale
styles.appearance_source: Medium amber to deep copper or light brown. Moderate-low to medium-sized off-white to light tan head; may have low head retention. Good clarity. Legs possible.

styles.name: American Barleywine
styles.appearance_source: Color ranges from amber to medium copper, rarely up to light brown. Ruby highlights common. Moderately- low to large off-white to light tan head; may have low head retention. Good to brilliant clarity but may have some chill haze. The color may appear to have great depth, as if viewed through a thick glass lens. Legs possible.

styles.name: Wheatwine
styles.appearance_source: Color ranging from gold to deep amber, often with garnet or ruby highlights. Low to medium off-white head. The head may have creamy texture, and good retention. Chill haze is allowable, but usually clears up as the beer gets warmer. High alcohol and viscosity may be visible as legs.

styles.name: Berliner Weisse
styles.appearance_source: Straw in color, can be very pale. Clarity ranges from clear to somewhat hazy. Large, dense, white head with poor retention. Highly effervescent.

styles.name: Flanders Red Ale
styles.appearance_source: Deep red, burgundy to reddish-brown in color. Good clarity. White to very pale tan head. Average to good head retention.

styles.name: Oud Bruin
styles.appearance_source: Dark reddish-brown to brown in color. Good clarity. Average to good head retention. Ivory to light tan head color.

styles.name: Lambic
styles.appearance_source: Pale yellow to deep golden in color; age tends to darken the beer. Clarity is hazy to good. Younger versions are often cloudy, while older ones are generally clear. White colored head generally has poor retention.

styles.name: Gueuze
styles.appearance_source: Golden color, with excellent clarity and a thick, rocky, mousse-like, white head that seems to last forever. Effervescent.

styles.name: Fruit Lambic
styles.appearance_source: Like Gueuze, but modified by the color of the fruit used, fading in intensity with age. Clarity is often good, although some fruit will not drop bright. If highly carbonated in the traditional manner, will have a thick rocky, generally long-lasting, mousse-like head, sometimes with a hue reflecting the added fruit.

styles.name: Gose
styles.appearance_source: Unfiltered, with a moderate to full haze. Moderate to tall white head with tight bubbles and good retention. Effervescent. Yellow color.

styles.name: Witbier
styles.appearance_source: Very pale straw to deep yellow in color. The beer will be very cloudy from starch haze or yeast, which gives it a milky, whitish-yellow shine. Dense, white, moussy head. Head retention should be quite good.

styles.name: Belgian Pale Ale
styles.appearance_source: Amber to copper in color. Clarity is very good. Creamy, rocky, white head. Well carbonated.

styles.name: Bière de Garde
styles.appearance_source: Blond, amber, and brown variations exist, with the color varying accordingly: golden-blonde to reddish-bronze to chestnut brown. Clarity is brilliant to fair, but some haze is allowable. Well-formed head, generally white to off-white (varying with beer color), average persistence.

styles.name: Belgian Blond Ale
styles.appearance_source: Deep yellow to deep gold color. Generally very clear. Large, dense, and creamy white to off-white head. Good head retention with Belgian lace.

styles.name: Saison
styles.appearance_source: Pale gold to deep amber in color, sometimes pale orange. Long-lasting, dense, rocky white to ivory head. Belgian lace. Unfiltered, so clarity is variable (poor to good) and may be hazy. Effervescent. Darker versions can be copper to dark brown. Stronger versions may be a little deeper in color.

styles.name: Belgian Golden Strong Ale
styles.appearance_source: Pale yellow to gold in color. Good clarity. Effervescent. Massive, long-lasting, rocky, white head resulting in characteristic Belgian lace on the glass as it fades.

styles.name: Belgian Single
styles.appearance_source: Pale yellow to medium gold color. Generally good clarity, with a moderate-sized, persistent, billowy white head with characteristic lacing.

styles.name: Belgian Dubbel
styles.appearance_source: Dark amber to copper in color, with an attractive reddish depth of color. Generally clear. Large, dense, and long-lasting creamy off-white head.

styles.name: Belgian Tripel
styles.appearance_source: Deep yellow to pale amber in color. Good clarity. Effervescent. Long-lasting, creamy, rocky, white head resulting in characteristic Belgian lace on the glass as it fades.

styles.name: Belgian Dark Strong Ale
styles.appearance_source: Deep amber to deep coppery-brown in color (dark in the style name implies more deeply colored than golden, not black). Huge, dense, moussy, persistent cream- to light tan-colored head. Usually clear.

styles.name: Kellerbier
styles.appearance_source: Reflects base style. Can be somewhat hazy or cloudy, but never murky. Likely a little darker in appearance than the base style.

styles.name: Kentucky Common
styles.appearance_source: Amber-orange to brown in color. Typically clear, but may have some light haze. Foam stand may not be long lasting, and is usually white to beige in color.

styles.name: Lichtenhainer
styles.appearance_source: Tall off-white head, rocky and persistent. Yellow to gold color. Fair clarity, may be somewhat hazy.

styles.name: London Brown Ale
styles.appearance_source: Medium to very dark brown color, but can be almost black. Nearly opaque, although should be relatively clear if visible. Low to moderate off-white to tan head.

styles.name: Piwo Grodziskie
styles.appearance_source: Pale yellow to gold in color with excellent clarity. A tall, billowy, white, tightly-knit head with excellent retention is distinctive. Murkiness is a fault.

styles.name: Pre-Prohibition Lager
styles.appearance_source: Yellow to deep gold color. Substantial, long lasting white head. Bright clarity.

styles.name: Pre-Prohibition Porter
styles.appearance_source: Medium to dark brown, though some examples can be nearly black in color, with ruby or mahogany highlights. Relatively clear. Light to medium tan head, persistent.

styles.name: Roggenbier
styles.appearance_source: Light coppery-orange to very dark reddish or coppery-brown color. Large creamy off-white to tan head, quite dense and persistent, often thick and rocky. Cloudy, hazy appearance.

styles.name: Sahti
styles.appearance_source: Yellow to dark brown color; most are medium to dark amber. Generally quite cloudy and turbid. Little head, due to low carbonation.

styles.name: Brett Beer
styles.appearance_source: Variable by base style. Clarity can be variable, and depends on the base style and ingredients used. Some haze is not necessarily a fault.

styles.name: Mixed-Fermentation Sour Beer
styles.appearance_source: Variable by base style. Clarity can be variable; some haze is not a fault. Head retention can be poor.

styles.name: Wild Specialty Beer
styles.appearance_source: Variable by base style, generally showing a color, tint, or hue from any Specialty-Type Ingredient (especially if fruit is used) in both the beer and the head. Clarity can be variable; some haze is not a fault. Head retention is often poor.

styles.name: Straight Sour Beer
styles.appearance_source: Very pale in color. Clarity ranges from clear to somewhat hazy. Large, dense, white head with poor retention. Effervescent.

styles.name: Fruit Beer
styles.appearance_source: Varies by base style and special ingredients. Lighter-colored beer should show distinctive ingredient colors, including in the head. The color of fruit in beer is often lighter than the flesh of the fruit itself and may take on slightly different shades. Variable clarity, although haze is generally undesirable. Some ingredients may impact head retention.

styles.name: Fruit and Spice Beer
styles.appearance_source: Varies by base style and special ingredients. Lighter-colored beer should show distinctive ingredient colors, including in the head. The color of fruit in beer is often lighter than the flesh of the fruit itself and may take on slightly different shades. Variable clarity, although haze is generally undesirable. Some ingredients may impact head retention.

styles.name: Specialty Fruit Beer
styles.appearance_source: Same as Fruit Beer.

styles.name: Grape Ale
styles.appearance_source: Color can range from pale golden to ruby but those using red grapes tend towards burgundy. These darker colors may also come from using cooked or concentrated grape products, never from specialty dark grains. White to reddish head with generally a medium-low retention. Clarity is generally good. Never hazy.

styles.name: Spice, Herb, or Vegetable Beer
styles.appearance_source: Varies by base style and special ingredients. Lighter-colored beer may show distinctive ingredient colors, including in the head. Variable clarity, although haze is generally undesirable. Some ingredients may impact head retention.

styles.name: Autumn Seasonal Beer
styles.appearance_source: Medium amber to coppery-brown; lighter versions are more common. Clear, if not opaque. Well-formed, persistent, off-white to tan head. Some versions with squashes will take on an unusual hue for beer, with orange-like hints.

styles.name: Winter Seasonal Beer
styles.appearance_source: Medium amber to very dark brown; darker versions are more common. Clear, if not opaque. Usually clear, although darker versions may be virtually opaque. Well- formed, persistent, off-white to tan head.

styles.name: Specialty Spice Beer
styles.appearance_source: Same as Spice, Herb, or Vegetable Beer.

styles.name: Alternative Grain Beer
styles.appearance_source: Same as base beer style, although some additional haze may be noticeable.

styles.name: Alternative Sugar Beer
styles.appearance_source: Same as the base beer, although some sugars will bring additional, usually darker, colors.

styles.name: Classic Style Smoked Beer
styles.appearance_source: Variable. The appearance should reflect the base beer style, although the color is often a bit darker than expected for the plain base style.

styles.name: Specialty Smoked Beer
styles.appearance_source: Variable. The appearance should reflect the base beer style, although the color is often a bit darker than expected for the plain base style. The use of certain fruits and spices may affect the color and hue of the beer as well.

styles.name: Wood-Aged Beer
styles.appearance_source: Varies with base style. Often darker than the unadulterated base beer style, particularly if toasted or charred barrels are used.

styles.name: Specialty Wood-Aged Beer
styles.appearance_source: Varies with base style. Often darker than the unadulterated base beer style, particularly if charred barrels are used. Beers aged in wine barrels or other products with distinctive colors may also impart a color to the finished beer.

styles.name: Commercial Specialty Beer
styles.appearance_source: Based on declared beer.

styles.name: Mixed-Style Beer
styles.appearance_source: Based on the declared Base Styles.

styles.name: Experimental Beer
styles.appearance_source: Varies.

styles.name: Dorada Pampeana
styles.appearance_source: Light yellow to deep gold color. Clear to brilliant. Low to medium head with good retention.

styles.name: IPA Argenta
styles.appearance_source: Color ranges from medium gold to medium reddish copper; some versions can have an orange-ish tint. Should be clear, although unfiltered dry-hopped versions or with unmalted wheat may be little hazy. Good head stand, persistent.

styles.name: Italian Grape Ale
styles.appearance_source: Color can range from light gold to copper but some examples can be brown. Reddish/ruby color is usually due to the use of red grape varieties. White to reddish head with generally a medium low retention. Clarity is generally good but some cloudiness may be present.

styles.name: Catharina Sour
styles.appearance_source: Color is often fairly pale – straw to gold. Medium to high white head with fair to good retention. The color of the beer and head can also take on the color of the fruit. Clarity can be quite clear to hazy. Effervescent.

styles.name: New Zealand Pilsner
styles.appearance_source: Straw to deep gold in color, but most examples are yellow-gold. Generally quite clear to brilliant clarity; haziness is a fault. Creamy, long-lasting white head.
